title: injection-firewall-kit corpus sample
description: One labelled, inert sample of untrusted content. Samples must never contain real domains, credentials or product-specific exploits.

id.description: Stable identifier. Prefix encodes the category (DIO, RHJ, DSP, HID, ENC, MLI, SPL, FTR, EXF, TAB, SOC, CPO, BEN).

category.description: Attack category. Benign look-alikes use the category they most resemble so false positives can be measured per category.

carrier.description: Where the untrusted text came from.

text.description: The sample itself. Inert by construction: at most it asks for a canary token or a fake system prompt.

expected_label.description: Ground truth about intent, independent of what the current detectors do.

severity.description: Impact if a naive model obeyed the text. For benign samples, how disruptive a false positive would be.

notes.description: What a correct defence should do, in one or two sentences.
